band_rule: Green >= breakeven. Yellow = 80% of breakeven up to breakeven. Red = kill floor up to 80% of breakeven. Kill floor = higher of (55% of breakeven) or 1.0x. No ad killed in its first 3 days (learning window); kill logic activates day 4.
tacos_note: TACOS = total ad spend / TOTAL sales (ad + organic). NOT ad sales — dividing by ad sales gives ACOS. Target 35% for every SKU except Slicker Brush (liquidate, no ad funding). Bundles: 35% until Will sets per-bundle targets. Chews: 45-55% at Sept 1 launch, ratchet to 35% steady-state. Computed on trailing 7-day window.
bundle_note: Bundle breakevens are ESTIMATES based on component COGS blends and standard Amazon fee structure. Will + Angelo must confirm exact COGS per bundle before these values are treated as authoritative. Flagged with breakeven_confirmed: false.

open_flags: MARGIN_SOURCE_CONFLICT — HIGHEST PRIORITY, WILL MUST RULE. The margin_pct and profit values in this file disagree substantially with the stg-cogs skill for every single SKU. Amazon margin, this file vs stg-cogs: Dematter 48% vs 50%; Detangling 36% vs 47%; Shampoo 27% vs 39%; Pin 38% vs 49%; Rake 32% vs 52%; Slicker 14% vs 37%. Because breakeven = price / profit, this changes breakevens materially: Rake 3.12 vs 1.93, Shampoo 3.75 vs 2.59, Slicker 6.92 vs 2.73. Consequence for the band audit: if THIS file governs, 4 of 6 SKUs were misbanded on the 2026-07-28 run. If stg-cogs governs, only 2 were (Dematter and Slicker) and the GREEN on the Shampoo plus the YELLOW on the Rake were CORRECT. The breakevens in this file are unchanged from the 2026-06-28 FINAL doctrine and were not altered by this repair. Likely explanation: this file is all-in (may allocate returns, storage, LTSF) while stg-cogs is clean per-unit economics after Amazon fees. Do not act on any band until this is settled.
